231	`renderProjectDetail` uses targeted DOM patching to avoid full-page flicker during poll cycles. Two strategies are applied depending on which data changed:
   232	
   233	```
   234	pollQueue() fires (every ~3 s while project detail is visible)
   235	  │
   236	  ├── Compute _orchRunsStructureKey(sorted, activeFilename)
   237	  │   → JSON string of sorted run filenames + activeFilename
   238	  │
   239	  ├── If key === lastRunsStructureKey (data-only change):
   240	  │   │   Same run list structure, same active run — only the status
   241	  │   │   card content may have changed (elapsed time, PID, progress).
   242	  │   │
   243	  │   └── _patchOrchStatusCard(matchingQueueEntry)
   244	  │       ├── Re-render OrchestratorWidgets.renderStatusCard()
   245	  │       ├── Replace innerHTML of #orch-status-card-container only
   246	  │       │   → Log preview widget (#orch-project-log-preview) is a
   247	  │       │     sibling — it is NOT touched
   248	  │       └── _pdLogPreviewCleanups array is NOT drained
   249	  │           → Existing log preview widget stays alive
   250	  │
   251	  └── If key !== lastRunsStructureKey (structural change):
   252	          Run appeared / run became inactive / first tick (key is null).
   253	          │
   254	          └── renderRunsList(matchingQueueEntry)
   255	              ├── Drain _pdLogPreviewCleanups (destroy existing widgets)
   256	              ├── Walk DOM from runsEl to find nearest scrollable ancestor
   257	              │   (window.getComputedStyle overflowY === 'auto'|'scroll')
   258	              │   → Falls back to document.documentElement if none found
   259	              ├── Save scrollTop of scroll anchor
   260	              ├── Rebuild runsEl.innerHTML (full structural re-render)
   261	              │   └── Active run section wraps status card in
   262	              │       <div id="orch-status-card-container">
   263	              ├── Restore scrollTop to saved value
   264	              └── Start new log preview widget (renderLogPreview)
   265	                  → Cleanup fn pushed into _pdLogPreviewCleanups
   266	```
   267	
   268	**Key invariants:**
   269	- `lastRunsStructureKey` is initialised to `null` so the first poll tick always takes the structural path and performs a full `renderRunsList`.
   270	- `_pdLogPreviewCleanups` is only drained on structural rebuilds — the log preview widget survives data-only status card updates.
   271	- `renderOrchToolbar` is called on every tick (both paths) to keep Kill/Resume button state current.
   272	
   273	---
   274	
   275	## 10. Project Name Cache Flow
   276	
   277	```
   278	View fetches project detail
   279	  │
   280	  ├── API.getProject(repo, slug) → { meta, project_name, ... }
   281	  │
   282	  ├── ProjectNameCache.set(makeProjectCacheKey(repo, slug), project_name)
   283	  │   → Stored for breadcrumb display
   284	  │
   285	  └── breadcrumb().project(repo, slug)
   286	      └── ProjectNameCache.get(key)
   287	          ├── If cached → return display name
   288	          └── If not cached → return slug portion (fallback)
   289	```

     4	
     5	## 1. No Build Step
     6	
     7	The frontend has **zero build tooling**. All `.js` and `.css` files in `public/` are served as-is by the static file server. There is no bundler, no minifier, no transpiler, no source maps.
     8	
     9	**Implications:**
    10	- Do not use `import`/`export` syntax in frontend files.
    11	- Do not use `let`, `const`, arrow functions, template literals, or other ES6+ features in frontend code.
    12	- Do not add a `package.json` to `gui/` or `gui/public/`.
    13	- Do not introduce webpack, vite, rollup, esbuild, or any bundler.
    14	- Cache-busting is done manually via `?v=N` query strings in `index.html` script/link tags.
    15	
    16	---
    17	
    18	## 2. ES5-Compatible JavaScript (Frontend)
    19	
    20	All frontend JavaScript uses **ES5-compatible patterns**:
    21	
    22	- `var` instead of `let`/`const`.
    23	- `function` declarations instead of arrow functions.
    24	- String concatenation instead of template literals.
    25	- IIFE module pattern instead of ES modules.
    26	- `Promise` chains with `.then()` / `.catch()` (native Promises are the one ES6 feature used, as all target browsers support them).
    27	
    28	**Exception:** `async/await` appears in `api-client.js` internal helper — this is acceptable because the GUI targets modern browsers where async/await has been supported since 2017.
    29	
    30	**Rationale:** The codebase was designed for maximum simplicity and zero dependencies. The pattern is intentional — do not "upgrade" to modern syntax without adding a transpilation step.
    31	
    32	---
    33	
    34	## 3. Global Namespace Pattern
    35	
    36	Frontend modules expose their public API as global variables via IIFEs:
    37	
    38	```javascript
    39	var ModuleName = (function () {
    40	  // private
    41	  return { publicMethod: fn };
    42	})();
    43	```
    44	
    45	**Rules:**
    46	- Each file exposes exactly one namespace (or a set of bare functions for `utils.js`).
    47	- Dependencies between modules are implicit (load order in `index.html` matters).
    48	- View files expose a `render*` function that the router calls.
    49	- Do not introduce a module loader or import map.
    50	
    51	---
    52	
    53	## 4. Hash-Based Routing Convention
    54	
    55	- All client-side routes use `#` prefix (e.g., `#/projects/repo/slug`).
    56	- The router matches routes via regex patterns in declaration order.
    57	- Route parameters are extracted via capture groups.
    58	- All URL parameters passed to API calls must be `encodeURIComponent()`-encoded.
    59	- New routes must be added to **both** `router.js` (dispatch) and the corresponding view file.
    60	
    61	---
    62	
    63	## 5. View Module Naming
    64	
    65	| Convention | Example |
    66	|------------|---------|
    67	| File name | `views/{noun}.js` (hyphenated) |
    68	| Render function | `render{PascalCase}(app, ...params)` |
    69	| First argument | Always the `#app` container element |
    70	| Pattern | `showLoading()` → fetch → build HTML string → set innerHTML |
    71	
    72	Views must:
    73	- Call `showLoading(app)` before any async work.
    74	- Handle fetch errors with `showError(app, message)`.
    75	- Use `breadcrumb()` for navigation context.
    76	- Cache project names via `ProjectNameCache.set()` when fetching project data.
    77	
    78	---
    79	
    80	## 6. CSS Theming System
    81	
    82	- All colors are defined as CSS custom properties on `:root`.
    83	- Dark mode overrides properties under `[data-theme="dark"]`.
    84	- Hard-coded hex values in dark overrides are acceptable (and necessary for specific badge backgrounds).
    85	- Never use hard-coded colors in the light-theme base styles — always reference `var(--color-*)`.
    86	- The `theme-init.js` script in `<head>` prevents FOUC by setting the attribute before body renders.
    87	
    88	---
    89	
    90	## 7. Security Constraints (Backend)
    91	
    92	### Path Traversal Prevention
    93	
    94	- All URL path parameters (slug, repo, wpId, filename) are validated against allowlist regexes before filesystem access.
    95	- `SAFE_SLUG_REGEX` (`/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/`) for project slugs and repo names.
    96	- `SAFE_ID_PATTERN` (`/^[A-Za-z0-9][\w-]*$/`) for WP IDs and queue entry IDs.
    97	- Static file serving checks `resolve(filePath).startsWith(PUBLIC_DIR)`.
    98	- Invalid parameters always return `NOT_FOUND` — never a different error that could leak information.
    99	
   100	### Body Size Limit
